regions.name: Packet Valley
regions.subject: Internet Technologies
regions.description: Follow one letter across a valley and see how the internet carries it: layers, wires, frames, addresses, routes, ports, web requests and security.
regions.bigFact: Nearly all data between continents travels through undersea cables, not satellites.

regions.name: Algo Archipelago
regions.subject: Algorithms and Complexity
regions.description: Island-hop through the ideas behind fast programs: how to organise data, count the cost of a method, and pick a smarter way to solve a problem.
regions.bigFact: Fold a sheet of paper in half 42 times and it would be thick enough to reach the Moon.

regions.name: Ledger Library
regions.subject: Databases
regions.description: Work the front desk of a grand library: how data is stored in tables, how keys link them, how to keep them tidy, and how SQL asks them questions.
regions.bigFact: Join a table of 1,000 members to a table of 1,000 loans with no matching rule and you get a million rows of nonsense.

regions.name: Blueprint Borough
regions.subject: Java
regions.description: Walk through a town of blueprints: how a Java program runs, how it stores values, makes decisions, repeats steps, and builds objects from classes.
regions.bigFact: In Java, 7 / 2 is 3, not 3.5, when both numbers are whole. The fraction is thrown away.

regions.name: Vault Harbour
regions.subject: Advanced Databases
regions.description: Work the docks of a busy harbour: how a database uses disks and memory, how a query is planned and costed, how indexes find rows fast, and how transactions keep the ledger right.
regions.bigFact: If every node in an index tree points to 100 children, a tree only four steps deep can reach 100 million nodes.

regions.name: Learning Fields
regions.subject: Machine Learning
regions.description: Help a farm learn from samples: how a computer finds patterns in examples, sorts by neighbours, trees and odds, fits lines and margins, and checks honestly that its predictions work.
regions.bigFact: A checker that never flags anything can still score 95 percent accuracy, if only 1 item in 20 is a problem. It also catches none of them.

regions.name: Wordwood
regions.subject: Natural Language Processing
regions.description: Wander a wood where the trees are words and the paths are sentences: how computers split and tidy text, count what comes next, sort and tag it, remember context, give words a place on a map and weigh every word against the rest.
regions.bigFact: Standard attention in a transformer compares every word with every other word, so doubling the length of a text makes that work grow four times.

regions.name: Waypoint Woods
regions.subject: AI Planning
regions.description: Walk forest trails where Kit plans each step to a goal: how a program searches for a route, writes a problem down, guesses the distance left, ignores what actions undo, and keeps only states with something new.
regions.bigFact: A world described by just 100 yes-or-no facts can be in up to about 10 to the power 30 different states, yet a width-1 search keeps at most 100 of them.
